_comment: What marks an observed row as a Flock Safety camera.
ssid_patterns: case-insensitive substrings matched against the SSID / device name.
oui_prefixes:  MAC prefixes, lower case and colon-separated, matched against the
start of the canonical BSSID. A full six-octet address is a legal
entry and matches that one device only — which is how every rule
here is written, on purpose. A three-octet vendor prefix would
match every gadget sharing that chip vendor, and this data already
contains the counter-example: the ESP32 Marauder's own Flock OUI
list includes 08:3a:88 (USI), which matches a resident's Ring
doorbell. Never add a bare vendor prefix.
PROVENANCE OF THE ENTRY BELOW (2026-09-22, confirmed by the owner):
The wardrive hardware is an ESP32 Marauder v1.17.0. Its Flock detector flags a
BLE device on XUNTONG manufacturer data (0xff 0xc8 0x09) plus a Penguin-style
name, OR on a MAC in a 27-entry OUI list (WiFiScan.h:862). A hit only increments
an on-screen counter — WiFiScan.cpp:702 — and the CSV row it writes has an empty
SSID field (WiFiScan.cpp:678), so no log can ever name a camera. The manufacturer
data is not in the CSV either, which leaves the MAC as the only replayable signal.
f0:82:c0:c1:fd:55 — Silicon Laboratories (a BLE beacon chip, consistent with a
Penguin battery pack). Seen on 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 within 6 m of the same
point, 34.06965/-117.19122: stationary across days, which is how a pole-mounted
camera behaves and not how a phone or a vehicle behaves. The owner confirmed the
camera and authorised publishing this marker.
A matching row is published to data/flock.json IN ADDITION to the database its
Type selects, so adding a rule never changes what the main map means. Delete a
rule and the marker stops being re-added; existing records are removed by hand,
the same way as a removal request (docs/removals.md).
